script: セイバールート十二日目-00
title: セイバールート十二日目-00

pages.ja:
ぺったんぺったん。
玉ねぎパン粉酒たまご塩、をこねくりまわした物と、挽肉四百グラムをこれまたコネコネとこねくり回す。
今朝のメニューは、大胆にも和風煮込みハンバーグに決定しました。

pages.en:
Pat, pat, pat.

I thoroughly knead together onions, breadcrumbs, sake, egg, and salt, then work the mixture into four hundred grams of ground meat.

In a daring departure from convention, this morning's menu shall be Japanese-style simmered hamburger steaks.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I start mixing.
I mix onion, breadcrumbs, alcohol, egg, and salt, and put it in with the beef and pork.
I’ve decided to cook Japanese-style hamburger for breakfast.

pages.ja:
「凛？ 目が覚めたのですか？」
居間からセイバーの声が聞こえる。
「遠坂？」
調理をしながら振り返る。

pages.en:
“Rin? Are you awake?”

Saber's voice reaches me from the living room.

“Tohsaka?”

I glance behind me as I cook.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Rin? Have you awoken?”
I can hear Saber’s voice from the living room.
“Tohsaka?”
I turn around while cooking.

pages.ja:
「……おはよ。ごめん、牛乳飲ませて士郎」
遠坂は不機嫌そうな顔でやってきて、冷蔵庫から牛乳を取り出した。
pages.jaRuby:
「……おはよ。ごめん、牛乳飲ませて士郎」
遠坂は不機嫌そうな顔でやってきて、冷蔵庫から牛乳を取り出した。
pages.en:
“…Morning. Sorry, Shirou. I need some milk.”

Wearing a thoroughly disagreeable expression, Tohsaka enters and takes the milk from the refrigerator.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Morning. Sorry, let me have some milk, Shirou.”
Tohsaka comes over with an unhappy face and takes some milk out of the refrigerator.

pages.ja:
「あー、寝過ぎて頭いたい……って、あれ？ なに、朝から凝ってるじゃない」
さっきまでの不機嫌っぷりは何処にいったのか、こっちを見るなり目を輝かす。
pages.jaRuby:
「あー、寝過ぎて頭いたい……って、あれ？ なに、朝から凝ってるじゃない」
さっきまでの不機嫌っぷりは何処にいったのか、こっちを見るなり目を輝かす。
pages.en:
“Ah, my head hurts from sleeping too long… Wait. What's this? You're making something elaborate this early?”

Her ill temper vanishes. The moment she sees what I am doing, her eyes light up.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Gah, my head hurts from sleeping too much… Hey, you sure are putting a lot of effort into breakfast.”
Where did that bad mood from earlier go? Her eyes gleam as soon as she turns to me.

pages.ja:
「へえ、おいしそう。うん、ちょうどお腹も減ってたし、助かったわ」
そうですか。だが助かったのはそっちで、助からなかったのはこっちだ。
切嗣の言っていた、どっちかが得をするとどっちかが損をする、とはこういうコトなのかもしれない。

pages.en:
“Oh, that looks delicious. Good. I was just getting hungry, so you've saved me.”

I see. Tohsaka may be saved, but I certainly am not.

Perhaps this is what Kiritsugu—my old man—meant when he said that for one person to gain, another must lose.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Wow, that looks good. I’m hungry so that’s really helpful.”
I see. But you’re the one that benefits, not me.
This must be what my father said… for someone to benefit, someone must lose.

pages.ja:
「……前から思ってたんだが。おまえ、わりと目ざといよな」
「あら、人並みに目端が利くだけよ。それじゃわたしの分もよろしくね」
pages.jaRuby:
「……前から思ってたんだが。おまえ、わりと目ざといよな」

pages.en:
“…I've thought this before, but you're remarkably quick to spot an opportunity.”

“Oh, only as quick as anyone else. I'll leave my portion in your hands.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I’ve thought so for a while, but you’re pretty sharp.”
“Oh, I’m only normally witted. So prepare some for me too.”

pages.ja:
ひらひらと手を振って居間に戻る。
遠坂は牛乳をついだグラスを片手に、テーブルにどかーっと陣取った。
……いや。
なんというか、すごい王様ぶりというか、気の抜けっぷりというか。

pages.en:
She waves airily and returns to the living room.

Holding a glass of milk in one hand, Tohsaka plants herself magnificently at the table.

…Well.

I cannot decide whether she looks like an arrogant king or simply a person who has abandoned all discipline.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Waving her hand, Tohsaka returns to the living room.
With a glass of milk in one hand, she takes position at the table.
…No.
Should I say she’s really relaxing or acting like royalty?

pages.ja:
「だらけていますね、凛」
よし、さすがセイバーだ。言いにくい事を実にハッキリと言ってくれる。
が。
セイバーの非難の目もどこ吹く風、まあねー、なんてやる気なさげに受け流していた。

が。

pages.en:
“You have grown terribly indolent, Rin.”

Excellent. I can depend upon Saber to state the difficult truth with perfect clarity.

But——

Saber's reproachful stare rolls harmlessly past Tohsaka. “I suppose I have,” she answers without the slightest energy.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“You are acting quite lazily, Rin.”
All right, way to go Saber. She sure is good at saying difficult things.
But…
Tohsaka waves off Saber’s criticism lazily like she doesn’t care.

pages.ja:
「そりゃあだらけもするわよ。
バーサーカーがいなくなった今、あとはキャスターとランサーとアサシンでしょ？ バーサーカーに比べたら大した敵じゃないし、今のセイバーなら余裕で撃退できるじゃない」
pages.jaRuby:
「そりゃあだらけもするわよ。
バーサーカーがいなくなった今、あとはキャスターとランサーとアサシンでしょ？ バーサーカーに比べたら大した敵じゃないし、今のセイバーなら余裕で撃退できるじゃない」
pages.en:
“Of course I'm taking it easy.

“Now that Berserker is gone, only Caster, Lancer, and Assassin remain, don't they? None of them compares to Berserker. Saber as she is now could drive them off without difficulty.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Of course I’m getting lazy.
Now that Berserker is gone, all that’s left are Caster, Lancer, and Assassin, right? They aren’t much compared to Berserker, and they can easily be fought off in Saber’s present condition.”

pages.ja:
「
それは判りません。ランサーもアサシンも一筋縄でいく相手ではない。
キャスターに至ってはまだ出会ってもいないではないですか」
pages.jaRuby:
「
それは判りません。ランサーもアサシンも一筋縄でいく相手ではない。
キャスターに至ってはまだ出会ってもいないではないですか」
pages.en:
“——We cannot know that. Neither Lancer nor Assassin is an opponent to be taken lightly.

“And we have yet even to encounter Caster.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I do not know.
Lancer and Assassin are not enemies
Lancer’s Master is still a mystery, and Assassin is not an enemy
that can be defeated by ordinary methods.
And we have not even met Caster yet.”

今までは魔力不足で嘆いてたけどそれも解決したし。
今のセイバーに対抗できるサーヴァントなんて一人もいないわ」

“Modesty, modesty. Before King Arthur, any ordinary Heroic Spirits may as well be bundled together.

“You spent all this time lamenting your lack of magical energy, but that problem has been solved.

“There isn't a Servant left who can stand against Saber now.”

“————”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Don’t be modest. A normal hero is an easy opponent for King Arthur, right?
You were grieving because you didn’t have enough magical energy, but that’s solved now.
There’s no Servant now that can match you, Saber.”
“”

pages.ja:
遠坂の言葉に、セイバーは目を細める。
……その気持ちは俺も同じだ。
今の遠坂の台詞は、さらりと聞き流せるものじゃない。
pages.jaRuby:

今の遠坂の台詞は、さらりと聞き流せるものじゃない。
pages.en:
Saber's eyes narrow at Tohsaka's words.

…I feel the same way.

What Tohsaka just said cannot be allowed to pass without comment.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Saber narrows her eyes at Tohsaka’s words.
…I feel the same way.
The thing Tohsaka just said can’t be ignored lightly.

pages.ja:
「
遠坂。おまえ、セイバーが誰かって気づいてたのか」
pages.jaRuby:
「
遠坂。おまえ、セイバーが誰かって気づいてたのか」
pages.en: “——Tohsaka. You realized who Saber is?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Tohsaka. You knew who Saber was?”

pages.ja:
「薄々ね。確信が持てたのは昨日よ。あれだけの聖剣を扱える英雄なんて一人しかいないもの。
……ま、伝説のアーサー王が女の子っていうのには驚いたけど、目の前にいるんじゃ信じるしかないじゃない」
pages.jaRuby:
「薄々ね。確信が持てたのは昨日よ。あれだけの聖剣を扱える英雄なんて一人しかいないもの。
……ま、伝説のアーサー王が女の子っていうのには驚いたけど、目の前にいるんじゃ信じるしかないじゃない」
pages.en:
“I suspected. Yesterday made me certain. Only one hero could wield a holy sword of that magnitude.

“…Admittedly, learning that the legendary King Arthur was a girl surprised me. But when she's standing in front of me, I have no choice but to believe it.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Vaguely. I only confirmed it yesterday. There’s only one hero who can use such a holy sword.
…Well, I was surprised that the legendary King Arthur is a girl, but if the real thing is in front of me, all I can do is believe it.”

pages.ja:
「それに伝説なんて都合よく改竄されたものでしょ？
セイバーが隠したのか周囲が隠したのか知らないけど、確かに中世の王様が女の子ってのは都合が悪いものね。
そりゃあ誰がなんと言おうと男として扱うわよ」
pages.jaRuby:
「それに伝説なんて都合よく[ruby text=かいざん char=2]改竄されたものでしょ？
セイバーが隠したのか周囲が隠したのか知らないけど、確かに中世の王様が女の子ってのは都合が悪いものね。
そりゃあ誰がなんと言おうと男として扱うわよ」
pages.en:
“Besides, legends are tampered with whenever it proves convenient, aren't they?

“I don't know whether Saber concealed it or whether the people around her did, but a medieval king being a girl would certainly have been inconvenient.

“No matter what anyone said, they would have treated her as a man.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“And legends usually are conveniently altered, right?
I don’t know if Saber hid it or the people around her hid it, but it certainly wasn’t convenient for a girl to be a king in the medieval times.
Of course they’d treat her as a man.”

pages.ja:
遠坂の口調はいつもと同じだ。
それを聞くセイバーも、特別気にした様子もない。
むしろ遠坂の意見に賛同し、否定しようとする気配もなかった。
pages.jaRuby:

むしろ遠坂の意見に賛同し、否定しようとする気配もなかった。
pages.en:
Tohsaka's voice is no different from usual.

Nor does Saber appear particularly troubled as she listens.

If anything, she seems to agree with Tohsaka and makes no move to contradict her.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Tohsaka has the same tone of voice as always.
Saber doesn’t seem to care that much either.
She rather seems to be agreeing with Tohsaka’s opinion and shows no sign of denying anything.

pages.ja:
「………………」
それは、彼女がはっきりと認めたという事だ。
セイバーのサーヴァントには、剣に関する英雄が選ばれる。その点で言えば、彼女はまさに最高のセイバーだろう。
pages.jaRuby:
「………………」
それは、彼女がはっきりと認めたという事だ。
セイバーのサーヴァントには、剣に関する英雄が選ばれる。その点で言えば、彼女はまさに最高のセイバーだろう。
pages.en:
“………………”

That amounts to an unmistakable admission.

Heroes associated with the sword are summoned into the Saber class. By that standard, she must surely be the greatest Saber imaginable.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“……”
So she has clearly admitted that it’s true.
A hero related to swords is chosen for the Servant Saber. From that perspective, she is certainly the best Saber there could be.

pages.ja:
英国における英雄の代名詞。
遠く離れたこの国でさえ名を知らぬ者のいない聖剣の担い手。
pages.jaRuby:
英国における英雄の代名詞。
遠く離れたこの国でさえ名を知らぬ者のいない聖剣の担い手。
pages.en:
The very embodiment of heroism in Britain.

The bearer of a holy sword whose name is known even in this distant country.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The great hero of England.
The bearer of the holy sword that everybody even in this distant country has heard of.

pages.ja:
……だが、だとするとどうなるのか。
アーサー王伝説の最後は、王の死で幕を閉じる。
いや、英雄であろうと人間だ。
その最期が死で終わるのは当然だが
まっとうな死を迎えた英雄などいない。
それはアーサー王とて例外ではなかった筈だ。

pages.en:
…But if that is true, what does it mean?

The legend of King Arthur closes with the king's death.

No—a hero is still human. Naturally, every life must end in death. But no hero ever meets an ordinary end.

King Arthur could not have been an exception.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…But if that’s the case, then what?
The end of the legend of King Arthur ends with the king’s death.
No, they are still human even though they are heroes.
It’s only natural for their last moment to end in death, but no hero dies normally.
King Arthur was no exception.

pages.ja:
アーサー王の最期は、たしか戦争による終わりだと記憶している。
カムランで起きた一大決戦。
ブリテンを統一し、倒すべき外敵がいなくなった筈のアーサー王は、その最後に思いもかけぬ『敵』と戦う事になる。

pages.en:
If I remember correctly, King Arthur met his end in war.

The great battle fought at Camlann.

After uniting Britain and defeating every foreign enemy, King Arthur faced an unexpected “enemy” at the very end.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I remember that the end of King Arthur was in a war.
The great battle of Camlann.
Having unified Britain and with no outside enemies to defeat, King Arthur faced an unexpected “enemy” in the end.

pages.ja:
それは守るべき自国の軍
腹心の裏切りによって、アーサー王は共に戦場を駆けてきた騎士たちに襲われ、これを殲滅したという。
pages.jaRuby:
それは守るべき自国の軍
腹心の裏切りによって、アーサー王は共に戦場を駆けてきた騎士たちに襲われ、これを殲滅したという。
pages.en:
It was the army of the country he was sworn to defend.

Betrayed by a trusted confidant, King Arthur was attacked by the very knights who had ridden beside him through countless battlefields—and annihilated them.
pages.mirrorMoon: The enemy was her own army that she protected. Because of a betrayal by the ones she trusted, King Arthur was attacked by the knights she had fought with, and it is said that the king had to defeat them.

pages.ja:
アーサー王は敵の頭を倒すものの致命傷を負い、ただ一人生き残った騎士であるベディヴィエールに聖剣の返上を託す。
“この血塗られた戦場を越え、丘を越えてくれ。
そこに深い湖がある。そこに、この剣を沈めるのだ”

pages.en:
King Arthur defeated the enemy commander, but suffered a mortal wound. To Bedivere, the only surviving knight, he entrusted the return of the holy sword.

“Cross this blood-soaked battlefield and go beyond the hill.

“There you will find a deep lake. Cast this sword into its waters.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
King Arthur succeeded in defeating the enemy leader, but took a fatal wound in the process and entrusted her only surviving knight, Sir Bedivere, with the return of the holy sword.
‘Go past this bloody battlefield and the hill.
There should be a lake there. Throw this sword into that lake.’

pages.ja:
しかしベディヴィエールはその言いつけを守れなかった。
一度目も二度目も、剣の損失を恐れたベディヴィエールは「剣は湖に捨てた」と偽りの報告をした。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
But Bedivere could not obey.

The first time and the second, fearing the loss of the sword, Bedivere returned and falsely reported that he had cast it into the lake.
pages.mirrorMoon:
But Bedivere could not follow the order.
Fearing the loss of the sword, Bedivere gave a false report the first and the second time, saying that he had thrown the sword into the lake.

pages.ja:
その度にアーサー王はベディヴィエールに剣の放棄を命じ、三度目にして王の命は守られた。
そうして、聖剣の返上が成った事を確かめたアーサー王は、その場で息を引きとったという。

pages.en:
Each time, King Arthur commanded Bedivere once more to relinquish the sword. On the third attempt, the king's order was finally obeyed.

And once assured that the holy sword had been returned, King Arthur drew his final breath where he lay.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Every time, King Arthur would order Bedivere to throw the sword away, and the order was followed on the third trip.
And it is said that King Arthur died after ascertaining that the holy sword had been returned.

pages.ja:
「それより士郎。アンタ、これからどうする気よ」
と。
唐突に、遠坂はこちらを睨んできた。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“More importantly, Shirou. What do you intend to do now?”

Without warning, Tohsaka turns a glare upon me.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“But anyway, what are you going to do now, Shirou?”
And then.
Tohsaka suddenly glares at me.

pages.ja:

放っておけって言ったのに、ここまで連れてきたのはアンタじゃない」

pages.en:
“What…? What do you mean, do about what?”

“The dangerous child sleeping in the Japanese room.

“I told you to leave her there, but *you* were the one who brought her all the way home.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Um… aboutwhat now?”
“About that dangerous child, who’s asleep right now.
You’re the one who brought her here, even though I told you to leave her behind.”

「そうそう、あんなのは綺礼に預けちまえばいいのよ」

「そうそう、あんなのは綺礼に預けちまえばいいのよ」
